TOP: GMO breach: 27,000 servers, $50M demand, customer data posted
Cloudflare GLM-5.3 cache leaked other customers' prompts
Microsoft Authenticator flaw hands out work tokens
AI agents get identity: IBM, Cisco, 1Password

P.h: Japan's GMO says hackers posted stolen customer data from 27,000 servers
P.p: GMO Internet says an attacker accessed its Onamae Desktop Cloud service for financial traders. Hackers demanded about $50 million, and GMO shut the service down on October 21. Customers report unauthorized trading-account activity, and alleged customer data has now appeared online.
P.s: GMO is verifying the leak, asking users to reset passwords and collecting customer devices to check for malware. Related: Keystone will destroy 18,835 hardware wallets after a stolen verification key.

items.h: Cloudflare GLM-5.3 cache bug returned other customers' data
items.d: Prompts over 681,280 tokens leaked other sessions in 155 responses via disaggregated SGLang. No deliberate exploitation found. Upgrade to SGLang 0.5.22 or later and check KV pool size per node.

items.h: Microsoft Authenticator for Android token theft flaw
items.d: A malicious app could impersonate trusted Microsoft apps and get work-account tokens with zero permissions. Fixed in 6.2606.4246 and later. Microsoft reports no known attacks.

items.h: AI-driven cloud attacks are loud, fast and persistent
items.d: Wiz walks through a real attack chain seen by its CIRT. Unify logs, assume full exposure on compromised resources and restrict trust between systems.

items.h: Context bombs cut AI attacker success sharply
items.d: Tracebit's 773 AWS runs: combined deception cut completed objectives from 2.48 to 0.23 per run and raised attacker cost 1.6 to 3.9 times.

P.h: Vendors race to give AI agents identities and short-lived access
P.p: IBM announced identity and control for AI agents at TechXchange, extending HashiCorp Vault to issue short-lived credentials for non-human identities. Cisco launched Privileged Infrastructure Access with task-specific privileges that expire once work is done.
P.s: TLDR IT also notes 1Password for Agents, which lets users approve agent sign-ins while it fills credentials directly into the site. Wiz data reported by TLDR DevOps ties this to stolen-token abuse.

tiles.t: Retire VPNs? Zero trust gains ground
tiles.d: Recurring gateway flaws plus AI-driven discovery push teams toward app-level access.

tiles.t: Linux EDR can look green while blind
tiles.d: Verify sensor health per host before expanding coverage.
Tighten access policies, disable unneeded SSH forwarding.
Partners Foxconn, Intel and Holcim show business context governing robots.

P.h: GitHub rebuilds Git writes for agent-scale traffic
P.p: GitHub is replacing repository-wide write serialization with per-reference quorums to overcome cross-region latency during its Azure migration. Internal tests showed 3 to 4 times higher throughput for writes to different references.
P.s: An object-storage-backed design lets read capacity scale independently. Gheist, covered by all three technical editions, shows why private repos and enterprise servers need token rotation.

tiles.d: Constrained decoding fixes 8% invalid calls seen in 0.28 for Kimi and DeepSeek.
Five building blocks, four rollout phases, OpenTofu Postgres example.
